findings.text: The corpus checks unsigned division for narrow and wide integer widths and for a divisor held in a register as well as a divisor encoded directly in the operation. Cases include small quotients and self division of extreme magnitudes that must produce unity, including the all bits set pattern divided by itself. One wide check loads the all ones pattern into two data registers, divides one by the other, compares against unity held in a third register, and reports success through the outcome register.

The corpus checks unsigned remainder with the same width and operand source combinations as division. Checked remainders include small residues and near maximum dividends that must leave small residues such as zero, one, or two. Both register sourced and directly encoded divisors appear for the narrow and wide forms.

Signed division and signed remainder reuse the unsigned division and remainder operations with an offset selector set to one. The range distinguishes the combinations of narrow versus wide width and register sourced versus directly encoded divisor for each signed operation, all validated with negative dividends such as negative six divided by two yielding negative three and negative seven remainder two yielding negative one.

The corpus checks bitwise conjunction, disjunction, and exclusive disjunction for narrow and wide widths with register sourced and directly encoded second operands. Narrow operations are expected to clear the upper half of the destination, while wide operations with a directly encoded operand apply sign extension of that operand before combining, as shown by paired low word expectations and full width comparison checks.

The corpus checks left shift with register sourced and directly encoded counts for both widths. Wide left shift is validated as a true sixty four bit operation by inspecting the low half directly and the high half after a following wide logical right shift by thirty two. Covered counts include zero, one, twelve, thirty one, exactly thirty two, and above thirty two such as thirty six.

Each test vector in this range carries a readable label describing operation, operands, and expected value, followed by a short internal instruction sequence that ends with an exit operation, a marker denoting internal execution, two empty slots, and an expectation pair keyed by channel zero that gives the required low word result. Longer checks needing full width comparison instead branch on equality between data registers and set the outcome register to one for success or two for failure before exiting.

The outcome of each program is observed in register R0, with the low thirty two bits compared against the expectation keyed by channel zero. Data setup uses registers R1 through R4, and conditional equality checks compare two data registers with a forward skip of two operations on success.

An implementer must preserve unsigned interpretation for division cases where the all ones bit pattern also reads as negative one. Under unsigned semantics the quotient of the all ones dividend by the all ones divisor is one, so a signed implementation or an overflow trap would produce the wrong result. Similarly narrow operations must discard high bits of widely loaded values before computing.
